compareCandidate.label: Xylem vs. phloem
compareCandidate.description: Xylem carries water and minerals upward, from root to leaf. Phloem carries food (sugar) from the leaves to the rest of the plant. They carry different materials in different directions.

processes: Supplying the leaves with water for photosynthesis
Water carrying up from root hairs to leaves
plainLanguageExplanation: Xylem is a transport tube that runs all the way through a plant, from the roots up the stem to the leaves. Its job is to carry water and dissolved minerals upward. It is made of a tissue of hollow tubes lined up end to end. Water enters the root in the root hairs the soil, then travels up the xylem and finally reaches the leaves, where it is used in photosynthesis. As water moves up some of it is also lost from the leaves.

keyFacts.label: Direction
keyFacts.value: Carries water and minerals upward, root to leaf

keyFacts.label: Material carried
keyFacts.value: Water and dissolved minerals from the soil

keyFacts.label: Structure
keyFacts.value: A tissue of joined tubes running the length of the plant

keyFacts.label: Starts
keyFacts.value: In the roots where water is absorbed

keyFacts.label: Ends
keyFacts.value: In the leaves, where water is used up and lost

whyItMatters: Every plant needs water, and xylem is the pipe that delivers it from the soil all the way to the leaves. Understanding xylem explains how water travels through a plant and how a tree keeps all its leaves watered high above the ground.
didYouKnow: Some xylem tubes run the full height of a tall tree, carrying water from deep in the ground up to the highest leaves.
